explanation: The task involves collecting two real crossings of a rubber cable cover on Rover C, comparing IMU spikes and wheel speeds, and delivering annotated plots. The setup is already prepared with the club rover, USB bridge, mat, and laptop. The core work consists of executing two trials, recording data, performing a specific comparison (signed difference between wheel-speed change and acceleration peak), and generating two annotated plots plus a paragraph. Since no comparable timed task exists in the history, this estimate relies on the assumption that data collection and basic analysis for two trials will take approximately 15 minutes per trial, totaling 30 minutes. This accounts for the setup time being minimal as the mat and laptop are already set up.
